comparison.objective: PR-618 fastens a screw and coupling nut through an upright plate until snug; the candidate loosens a captive collar setscrew, adjusts damping, relocks it, and validates the setting through repeated impacts.
comparison.physical_skill: Both require bimanual counterholding, axial tool/fastener alignment, rotation, and controlled tightening. PR-618 additionally coordinates loose screw/nut insertion through a plate and thread capture; the candidate instead requires withdrawing/re-engaging a hex bit on a moving collar and iteratively selecting a setting from dynamic response.
comparison.success_condition: PR-618 requires passage through the plate, thread catch, ≥1.5 turns, ≤2 mm combined stand-off, release, and 1 s stillness. The candidate requires two impact cycles within published energy/velocity/stroke constraints, no hard-stop strike or overload, and retained collar setting. Candidate rebound, overload, drift, and witness-torque thresholds are not yet numeric.
comparison.reason: This is the closest record at the primitive level, but fastening two loose parts through a plate tests assembly/thread capture, while the candidate tests adjustment retention plus closed-loop dynamic commissioning. The defining outcomes are materially different.
